'''Pranab Kumar Sen''' (7 November 1937 – 31 December 2023) was an Indian-American [[statistician]] who was a professor of statistics and the Cary C. Boshamer Professor of Biostatistics at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pranab K. Sen Obituary {{!}} UNC Statistics & Operations Research |url=https://stor.unc.edu/news-item/pranab-sen-obituary/ |access-date=1 February 2024 |website=stor.unc.edu}}</ref><ref name="profile">[https://stat-or.unc.edu/people/faculty/pranab-sen Faculty profile], UNC Chapel Hill, retrieved 3 July 2011.</ref>

==Biography==
Pranab Kumar Sen was born in [[Calcutta]], [[Bengal Presidency]], [[British India|India]] on 7 November 1937,<ref name="cv">[http://www.sph.unc.edu/images/stories/cv_storage/704289903_cv.pdf Curriculum vitae] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720092739/http://www.sph.unc.edu/images/stories/cv_storage/704289903_cv.pdf |date=20 July 2011|url-status=dead}}, retrieved 3 July 2011.</ref> as the second of seven siblings. His father, a railway officer, died of leukemia when Sen was ten, and he was raised by his mother, the daughter of a [[physician]].<ref name="gs08"/> He began his undergraduate studies at [[Presidency University, Kolkata|Presidency College, Kolkata]], initially intending to study medicine but shifting to statistics when it was discovered that he was too young for medical college.<ref name="gs08"/> He received a B.S. from the [[University of Calcutta]] in 1955, an M.Sc. in 1957, and a Ph.D. in 1962;<ref name="cv"/><ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Pranab Kumar Sen|id=18736}}.</ref> his [[doctoral advisor]] was Hari Kinkar Nandi.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1990 |title=H. K. Nandi's Contributions to Statistics–An Appreciation |url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0008068319900503 |journal=[[Calcutta Statistical Association Bulletin]] |language=en |volume=40 |issue=1–4 |pages=1–22 |doi=10.1177/0008068319900503 |issn=0008-0683|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name="gs08"/> He taught for three years at the University of Calcutta and one more year at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] before joining the UNC faculty in 1965; although he has held visiting positions at other universities, he remained at Chapel Hill for the rest of his career.<ref name="cv"/><ref name="profile"/> He was the founding co-editor of two journals, ''Sequential Analysis'' and ''Statistics and Decisions'',<ref name="gs08"/> and was joint editor-in-chief of the ''Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference'' from 1980 to 1983.<ref name="cv"/>

Sen died in [[Chapel Hill, North Carolina]] on 31 December 2023, at the age of 86.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pranab K. Sen Obituary |url=https://stor.unc.edu/news-item/pranab-sen-obituary/ |website=UNC |access-date=5 February 2024 |date=20 January 2024}}</ref>

==Research and graduate advising==
Sen was the author or co-author of multiple books on [[non-parametric statistics]], the advisor of over 80 Ph.D. students, and the author of over 600 research publications.<ref name="cv"/><ref name="bps08"/> He is known for inventing the [[Hodges–Lehmann estimator]] independently of and contemporaneously with Hodges and Lehmann<ref name="gs08"/><ref>{{cite book| last=Lehmann|first=Erich&nbsp;L.|author-link=Erich Leo Lehmann|title=Nonparametrics: Statistical methods based on ranks|edition=Reprinting of&nbsp;1988 revision of&nbsp;1975 Holden-Day | publisher=Springer | location=New&nbsp;York|year=2006|isbn=978-0-387-35212-1|pages=176 and&nbsp;200–201|mr=395032}}</ref> and for the [[Theil–Sen estimator]], a form of [[robust regression]] that fits a line to two-dimensional sample points by choosing the slope of the fit line to be the median of the slopes of the lines through pairs of samples.<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Rousseeuw | first1 = Peter J. | author1-link = Peter Rousseeuw
 | last2 = Leroy | first2 = Annick M.
 | isbn = 978-0-471-48855-2
 | title-link = Robust Regression and Outlier Detection
 | publisher = Wiley
 | series = Wiley Series in Probability and Mathematical Statistics
 | title = Robust Regression and Outlier Detection
 | at = [https://books.google.com/books?id=lK9gHXwYnqgC&pg=PA67 p. 67]
 | volume = 516
 | year = 2003}}.</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Wilcox | first = Rand R.
 | contribution = Theil–Sen estimator
 | isbn = 978-0-387-95157-7
 | pages = 207–210
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag
 | title = Fundamentals of Modern Statistical Methods: Substantially Improving Power and Accuracy
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=YSFb4QX2UIoC&pg=PA207
 | year = 2001}}.</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Sen was a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]<ref>[http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm IMS Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302125855/http://www.imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm |date=2 March 2014 }}, retrieved 3 July 2011.</ref> and of the [[American Statistical Association]] (ASA).<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/careers/fellowslist.cfm ASA Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200409223154/http://www.amstat.org/careers/fellowslist.cfm |date=9 April 2020 }}, retrieved 3 July 2011.</ref> He became the Cary C. Boshamer Professor in 1982.<ref name="cv"/> He was the [[Lukacs Distinguished Professor|Lukacs Distinguished Visiting Professor]] at [[Bowling Green State University]] in 1996–1997.<ref>[http://bayes.bgsu.edu/lukacs/lukacs_profs.html Bowling Green State University: Eugene Lukacs Professors] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110812062403/http://bayes.bgsu.edu/lukacs/lukacs_profs.html |date=12 August 2011 }}, retrieved 3 July 2011.</ref> In 2002, he won the [[Gottfried E. Noether Awards|Gottfried E. Noether Senior Scholar Award]] of the ASA,<ref>[http://www.amstat.org/careers/gottfriednoetherawards.cfm Gottfried E. Noether Awards], retrieved 3 July 2011.</ref> and he was the 2010 winner of its [[Wilks Memorial Award]] "for outstanding contributions to statistical research, especially in nonparametric statistics and biostatistics; and for exceptional service in mentoring doctoral students."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sph.unc.edu/sph-news/unc-gillings-community-mourns-professor-emeritus-pranab-sen/|title=UNC Gillings community mourns Professor Emeritus Pranab Sen|date=January 5, 2024|publisher=UNC Gillings School of Public Health|access-date=2024-04-12}}</ref> In 2012, the [[University of Calcutta]] awarded him an [[List of University of Calcutta honorary degree recipients|honorary Doctor of Science]] degree.<ref>{{cite web|title=Annual Convocation|url=http://www.caluniv.ac.in/convocation-2012/hony_degrees.htm|publisher=[[University of Calcutta]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120528004638/http://caluniv.ac.in/convocation-2012/hony_degrees.htm|archive-date=28 May 2012}}</ref>
